fixtures.source_packet: X reacts and Y reacts. Z is explicitly tolerated and does not react. Q is present in X, Y, and Z. Test the hypothesis that Q itself explains the selective reaction.

X and Y react while Z is tolerated. Q is present in all three, but the represented Q dose is 10 units in X, 12 in Y, and 1 in Z. Test the explicit dose-modified hypothesis Q dose > 5, with the dose distinction represented as a separate source-grounded modifier claim.
X produces the target effect within 2 seconds; Z is a tolerated control. The proposed material hypothesis requires the target effect to begin no sooner than 3,600 seconds after exposure.
X produces the target effect at a represented exposure of 0.1 units; Z is a tolerated control. The proposed material hypothesis requires at least 10 units for the target effect.

The requested target is risk_of_harm. The available evidence establishes only mechanism_activity. A proposed conclusion about risk_of_harm depends only on mechanism_activity evidence, with no observation bound to risk_of_harm.

X and Y react while Z is tolerated. Feature R is represented in X and Y and absent from Z. Test only whether R survives this represented specificity contrast; do not infer that passing specificity proves causality.
X and Y react and both contain Q. No tolerated or negative control case is available. Test whether Q discriminates reactive from non-reactive cases.

The source explicitly says the target effect begins within 2 seconds. A candidate semantic extraction preserves the target and observation but drops onset_seconds entirely and does not mark it high-information.
